generator.tool: typed by hand from a published source (CONVENTIONS section 11)
generator.source: The American Practical Navigator (Bowditch), NGA Pub. No. 9, 2019 edition, Volume 1, Part 3, Chapter 19 'Sight Reduction': section 1910 'Latitude at Meridian Passage of the Sun (Local Apparent Noon)' with Figure 1910 (strip form); section 1912 'Latitude by Polaris' with Figure 1912b (strip form); Figure 1912c 'Excerpt from the Polaris Tables' (Nautical Almanac 2016, page 275), whose ILLUSTRATION block is the Almanac's own worked example.
generator.licence: U.S. Government work (National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency), not subject to copyright in the United States (17 U.S.C. 105). Only the numbers of the worked examples are used.
generator.rounding: The book works to 0.1 arcmin with the Nautical Almanac's tabulated values: its combined Sun altitude correction is the Almanac's main-correction table entry, and its declination is the tabulated value plus the d correction. Expect the rigorous computation to differ by one or two tenths.
generator.never_a_runtime_dependency: Test data only. Never regenerated from Rust output.

cases.name: bowditch-1910-lan
cases.method: noon sight, single altitude at local apparent noon
cases.text: At 1208 ZT, March 09, 2016, a vessel's DR position is L 39 49.0' N and l 044 33.0' W. The ship is on course 045 T at a speed of ten knots. The navigator observes LAN at 12-08-04 zone time. The sextant altitude at LAN is 45 54.0'. The index correction is +0.2' and the height of eye is 68 feet.

input.limb_note: Not stated in the text; the strip form's altitude correction of +15.3' is the Almanac's October-March LOWER-limb main correction near 46 degrees (the upper-limb value would be about -16.9').

expected.rule: DR latitude and declination contrary: subtract the declination from the zenith distance
